# now

## R-0003 · Prove sbx --seccomp end to end through bwrap on a Linux host

state: active
horizon: now
origin: docs/adr/0005-approve-the-wrapper-not-the-command.md#consequences
blocked_by: []
tags: [sandbox]

The x86_64 syscall allowlist behind sbx --seccomp shipped (see ADR 0005's R-0003 addendum) and was validated in-process with prctl on t42, but the real path -- bwrap receiving the program via --seccomp FD and installing it -- is unproven. t42 cannot run it: bubblewrap is not installed, unprivileged_userns_clone=0 and apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1. Needs a Linux x86_64 host with a working bwrap: run seccomp_probe.py under sbx --seccomp, compare with a control run without the flag, clean up.

## R-0004 · Let the implement skill route a failed task to Quint

state: idea
horizon: later
origin: docs/adr/0006-the-second-executor.md#consequences
blocked_by: []
tags: [agents, skills]

Under /p:implement a failing task still only reaches Watson, because Mason may not spawn another executor. The intended bridge is the skill calling Quint, deliberately left unbuilt.

## R-0017 · DDG planned investigation (TLS capture diff, byte-identical handshake, __sc__ fingerprint)

state: idea
horizon: later
origin: docs/concepts/spec-ddg.md#82-planned-investigation

Three planned investigations into DDG's bot detection: capture and diff raw TCP/TLS between Chrome and curl_cffi (mcp-tshark now exists), build a byte-identical browser handshake via an external library, and replicate the __sc__ DOM fingerprint for the main endpoint.
